finding: The runtime view says that 'dispatch close --orphans cleans up worktrees, branches, and ledgers that no active run owns (BR-120)'. Commit 28ec0830 splits that rule. BR-120 now holds only the ledgers, and the new BR-125 holds the worktrees of no ledger. BR-125 also says that --orphans lists the branch of each such worktree and deletes no branch. So the sentence names a cleanup of branches that does not happen, and it cites only one of the two rules. Change the sentence to: 'dispatch close --orphans removes the ledgers that no active run owns (BR-120) and the merged worktrees that no ledger owns (BR-125). It deletes no branch.' Owner: architecture-agent.
why_this_severity: BR-120, BR-125 and the close bullet of the interface contracts state the rule, and the code follows them, so a planner or implementer reaches the right behavior (no to fails_purpose); a reader of the runtime view expects branches to go and must read BR-125 to learn otherwise (raises_cost). No story or code outside the run encodes the sentence.
